confirmed.proposal: Add `FEAT_PICK_GRANTS['experimental-spellshaping'] = { prompt: 'Choose a 1st-level spellshape wizard feat', category: 'class', maxLevel: 1, traits: ['wizard','spellshape'] }` in src/rules/featPickGrants.ts, and make the class-feature pick walk see thesis answers: src/rules/build.ts ~4644 iterates `classFeatureIdsOwned(build, content)` with a BuildState, which has no `classChoices`, so extraChoices answers (the thesis) never enter that set — pass `classChoices: grantOptions.map((o) => ({ id: o.id, level: 1 }))` there the way lines 4751 / 4972 / 5832 / 5936 already do. For the 4th-level clause add a src/rules/dailyChoices.ts entry keyed on the same id with a half-level feat filter (WG approximates it with a static level-10 cap; a `maxLevel: 'half'` spec matches print exactly).
confirmed.evidence: AoN arcane-thesis-6 (Player Core pg. 195) prints both clauses verbatim as quoted. Our classFeatures['experimental-spellshaping'] is bare of every grant field (id/name/traits/rarity/source/level/actionCost/otherTags/edition/aonId only) and the thesis option in classes.wizard.extraChoices[0] carries just id/name/description, while its siblings do carry mechanics (improved-familiar-attunement has grantsFeats:['familiar'] + COMPANION_GRANTS at companionGrants.ts:144, staff-nexus has grantsItems + two effectChoices). `grep -rn experimental-spellshaping src/` returns ZERO hits — no FEAT_PICK_GRANTS, no dailyChoices, no featFeatGrants entry — and its only occurrence outside core.json is an edition:'remaster' row in effect-backfill.json. The mechanism claim also holds: build.ts:4645 calls classFeatureIdsOwned(build, …) with a BuildState, and derive.ts:3246 only adds ids from `opts.classChoices`, which BuildState never carries (lines 4751/4972/5832/5936 pass grantOptions explicitly, 4645 does not), so a thesis id could not reach the pick walk even if a spec existed. Their side: wg-show --wgid 34149 prints the level-max-1 Wizard+Spellshape select plus the LEVEL>=4 conditional select.

confirmed.claim: Print gives every necromancer the Command a Thrall action at 1st level, but on our side (and on WG's) the action is handed out only by the Necromancer Dedication archetype feat — so a base necromancer never gets it on the sheet while an archetype dabbler does.
confirmed.printed: "A thrall has a Speed of 15 feet unless otherwise noted. You can use the Command a Thrall action (see below) as long as you have at least one thrall. When you Command a Thrall to Strike, it makes a melee unarmed Strike using your spell attack modifier for its attack roll. This Strike uses and counts toward your multiple attack penalty. The Strike deals 1d6 bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage. At 5th level and every 4 levels thereafter, the damage increases by 1d6." / "**Command a Thrall** [Single Action] (concentrate, necromancer, thrall) You make one of your thralls Crawl, Drop Prone, Escape, Interact, Stand, Stride, or Strike." (AoN class-75, Key Terms aside)
confirmed.ours: actions['command-a-thrall'] exists and its description in public/core-descriptions.json even carries the damage ladder ("…dealing 1d6 bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage; at 5th level and every 4 levels thereafter the damage increases by 1d6"). But the only `grantsActions` naming it anywhere in core.json is on the ARCHETYPE feat: feats['necromancer-dedication'] = { …, "grantsActions":["command-a-thrall"], "focusSpells":["create-thrall"] }. classes.necromancer carries no grantsActions, and none of its 19 features does either — classFeatures['grave-spells'] (which is the feature that hands over create thrall and thrall charge) has only `note`. The granted-action walk (src/rules/build.ts ~5501, `for (const a of g.grantsActions ?? [])`) therefore never reaches it for a base necromancer.
confirmed.theirs: Same gap, so this is a residual read rather than a parity adoption: ability_block 57836 "Command a Thrall" (type=feat, level=1, operations=[]) is referenced by exactly ONE giveAbilityBlock in the whole dump — ability_block 57851 "Necromancer Dedication": {"type":"giveAbilityBlock","data":{"type":"feat","abilityBlockId":57836}}. Their necromancer class row (class id 337) and every necromancer class-feature row (Grave Spells 57685 gives only spellId 8763/8770/8754, Fatal Method 57684, Grim Fascination 57683) grant nothing of the kind.
confirmed.proposal: Add `grantsActions: ["command-a-thrall"]` to classFeatures['grave-spells'] — the 1st-level feature whose Grave Cantrips clause already delivers create thrall and thrall charge, i.e. the first thing that gives a necromancer a thrall to command — mirroring the wording already on feats['necromancer-dedication'].
confirmed.evidence: AoN class-75 (Impossible Magic) carries the thrall key-terms text "You can use the Command a Thrall action (see below) as long as you have at least one thrall" plus the [Single Action] (concentrate, necromancer, thrall) stat block — a chassis benefit, not a feat. A full value walk of public/core.json finds the string 'command-a-thrall' in exactly two places: actions.command-a-thrall.id and feats['necromancer-dedication'].grantsActions[0]; classes.necromancer has no grantsActions and none of its 19 features does (grave-spells carries only a `note`). The sheet's action list (src/sheet/MainTab.tsx:281-330) is assembled from feats + owned class features + ancestry/heritage/background/held items via grantsActions plus character.grantedActionIds, so nothing puts it on a base necromancer — who does get thralls, since classes.necromancer.focusSpells = ['necrotic-bomb','create-thrall','thrall-charge']. Their dump agrees it is a residual read, not a parity adoption: 57836 appears 5× and the only giveAbilityBlock pointing at it sits in Necromancer Dedication; the rest are prose links. Note the fix lands on a class FEATURE record, not the class record.

refuted.claim: We offer Bloodrager as an ungated 1st-level instinct, but its printed text replaces the barbarian's entire starting skill block (Athletics + Medicine + 2 + Int) and requires Bloodrager Dedication as the 2nd-level class feat; neither our record nor WG models either half.
refuted.printed: Bloodrager Adjustments: You are trained in Athletics, Medicine, and a number of additional skills equal to 2 plus your Intelligence modifier, instead of your normal starting skill proficiencies. You must choose the bloodrager instinct for your barbarian instinct. … You must select Bloodrager Dedication as your 2nd-level class feat. Prerequisites: You must be a barbarian. (carried verbatim in our own classes.barbarian subclass option 'bloodrager'; printed source is the Bloodrager class archetype, aon-2e-archive/data/by-category/archetype/archetype-283.json — class-57's own text only points at Instincts.aspx)
refuted.ours: classes.barbarian.subclass.options[] entry is `{"id":"bloodrager","name":"Bloodrager"}` — no `grants`, no prerequisite gate, and no per-option skill override. classes.barbarian.trainedSkills stays {fixed:['athletics'], additional:3} for every instinct. src/rules/build.ts:3121 reads only `o.grants?.skills` from a subclass option (`for (const sk of o.grants?.skills ?? []) (skills[sk] = 'trained'), lock(sk, 'a class choice')`), and the skill count comes from `additionalClassSkills(build, content)` off the class-level `trainedSkills.additional` with no option-level override anywhere. A Bloodrager barbarian therefore builds with Athletics + 3 + Int and no Medicine, and can be built without ever taking Bloodrager Dedication.
refuted.theirs: Bloodrager Instinct (their id 51667, type=feat, level=1) encodes only combat mechanics — `setValue variable=RAGE_DAMAGE value=4` / `value=8` under level and greater-weapon-specialization conditionals, three `adjValue variable=RESISTANCES` entries under `IF ACTIVE_MODES INCLUDES rage / IF LEVEL GREATER_THAN_OR_EQUALS 9`, `addBonusToValue variable=MELEE_ATTACK_DAMAGE_BONUS value={{rage_damage/2}} type=persistent bleed`, and an injectText of the instinct ability. No SKILL_ op, no skill-count op, no prerequisite op. Their Barbarian class row (id 108) hard-sets skill_training_base=3 and SKILL_ATHLETICS T unconditionally.
refuted.proposal: On classes.barbarian.subclass.options 'bloodrager', add `grants:{skills:['athletics','medicine']}` (already read at src/rules/build.ts:3121) plus a new per-option starting-skill override — e.g. `trainedSkillsOverride:{fixed:['athletics','medicine'], additional:2}` — read alongside `cls.trainedSkills` in `additionalClassSkills` and at src/rules/build.ts:3121; and gate the option on the Bloodrager Dedication feat so the instinct cannot be chosen without it.
refuted.evidence: The finding's decisive "ours" claim — "builds with Athletics + 3 + Int and no Medicine" — is false: src/rules/featGrantsAuto.ts:118 carries `'bloodrager': { skills: { athletics: 'trained', medicine: 'trained' } }`, it reaches a build because derive.ts:3242 adds the subclass id itself to classFeatureIdsOwned (classFeatures['bloodrager'] exists) and build.ts:4967-4976 feeds those ids to FEAT_GRANTS, so a real level-1 bloodrager barbarian I built came out Athletics + Medicine trained while a fury-instinct barbarian got Athletics only — the proposal's `grants:{skills:['athletics','medicine']}` would re-author a grant that already fires. The print quote itself is genuine (archetype-283, War of Immortals p. 60, and our option's description carries it verbatim), and a narrower residue does survive: additionalClassSkills(build) still returns 3 where print says 2 (one skill too many, not a missing one), and SubclassOption has no prerequisite field so nothing gates the instinct on Bloodrager Dedication — re-file that as a two-line finding if the parent wants it, but the finding as written breaks.

refuted.claim: The witch prepares from her FAMILIAR's known spells, not from the whole tradition list; our chassis encodes the identical shape as the cleric and druid, so a witch can prepare any primal/occult/etc. spell in the game.
refuted.printed: Witch Spellcasting: "At 1st level, you can prepare up to two 1st-rank spells and five cantrips each morning from the spells your familiar knows." Familiar → Spells: "Your familiar is the source and repository of the spells your patron has bestowed upon you, and you must commune with your familiar to prepare your spells each day using your witch spellcasting. Your familiar starts off knowing 10 cantrips, five 1st-rank spells, and one additional spell determined by your patron's initial lesson. … Each time you gain a level, your patron teaches your familiar two new spells of any rank for which you have spell slots". (AoN class-38)
refuted.ours: classes.witch.spellcasting = {"type":"prepared","tradition":"arcane","keyAbility":"int","repertoire":false} — byte-for-byte the same shape as classes.druid ({prepared, primal, wis, repertoire:false}) and classes.cleric. src/rules/build.ts:3711 branches only on `sp.repertoire`, so there is no known-list notion at all; the prepare picker offers the whole tradition.
refuted.theirs: Baba Yaga (their id 40527): {"type":"defineCastingSource","data":{"variable":"CASTING_SOURCES","value":"WITCH:::PREPARED-LIST:::OCCULT:::ATTRIBUTE_INT"}} (each patron restates it with its own tradition), against Druid Spellcasting's "DRUID:::PREPARED-TRADITION:::PRIMAL:::ATTRIBUTE_WIS" and Cleric Spellcasting's "CLERIC:::PREPARED-TRADITION:::DIVINE:::ATTRIBUTE_WIS". This distinction is NOT covered by scripts/wg-casting.mjs, whose TOKEN_TYPE map (line 97) collapses 'PREPARED-TRADITION' and 'PREPARED-LIST' to the same 'prepared'.
refuted.proposal: Add a known-list flag to ClassDef.spellcasting (e.g. `preparedFrom: 'list'` alongside `repertoire`) and gate the witch's prepare picker on the familiar's learned spells — 10 cantrips + five 1st-rank at L1, +2 of any castable rank per level, plus the patron's lesson spell (witch#patron-familiar-spell). Reader: src/rules/build.ts:3711.
refuted.evidence: The chassis JSON is indeed shaped like the druid's, but the conclusion is false: build.ts has an explicit `} else if (cls.id === 'wizard' || cls.id === 'witch') {` branch (line 3747) — "LEARNED prepared casters — build.spells is a SPELLBOOK of known spells (the wizard's physical spellbook; the witch's familiar, 'the source and repository of the spells your patron has bestowed')" — which sets entry.spellbook and fills entry.prepared from `learned` only. The sheet's prepare picker honours it: SpellsTab.tsx optionsFor() line 654 `if (entry.spellbook) { … return out; }` returns spellbook spells only, never traditionSpellsByRank. The builder gates the witch through the same lane (Builder.tsx:389 `isWizardBook = … (casterCls?.id === 'wizard' || casterCls?.id === 'witch')`) with wizardSpellbookBudget → spellcasting.ts:174 `5 + 2 * (level - 1)`, which is print's witch rule verbatim (five 1st-rank at L1, two new per level). The claim's cited line 3711 (`if (sp.repertoire)`) is only the first branch of a three-way; it is not the whole dispatch. (Residual, out of this claim's scope: our cantrip lane is 5, print says the familiar knows 10 cantrips.)
